about: How original state (Ghidra slot keys) maps onto the C++ port's GameState, for microexec's port comparison. Read by bridge.py; the host reflects every public port field and every @port-cited function (host/gen_reflection.py), so a port path is any GameState member path. See tools/microexec_evnova/README.md. A `skip` drops a slot the port does not read and still compares the run; an `unmapped` reason makes the run not-comparable because the port cannot be given that state. With `auto`, a slot with no explicit rule is checked against the host's port records: a field keeps its name, or a numbered field maps into the one array its stem pluralizes to (class_1 -> classes[0]); a scalar argument keeps its name (or its position), and `arg.<ptr>[*].<field>` becomes `<port param>.<field>`. Every target the host can call is compared without a `targets` entry. Only renames, skips, not-comparables and argument overrides need writing down.

g_reaction_script_buffer.skip: Expression/script scratch storage is local string storage in the port; gameplay effects are compared separately.

g_pers_defs.why: Fixed 0x400 personality table indexed by resource id minus 0x80 in both implementations.

g_system_reputation.why: Per-system int16 reputation, indexed by the same zero-based system id.

g_active_misn.why: Accepted mission slots retain the original indexing and ship goal/behavior fields.

g_active_misn_runtime_flags.why: Separate 20-byte runtime records for the same 16 accepted mission slots.

g_random_encounter_fleet_defs.why: Fixed 0x100 fleet table with a 0x124 stride; government ids are zero-based in both implementations.

g_system_defs_ptr[*].reinf_countdown.why: Mutable SystemDef +0xc8 lives in a separate per-system array in GameState.

g_system_defs_ptr[*].reinf_cooldown_days.why: Mutable SystemDef +0xc4 lives in a separate per-system array in GameState.

g_player_reinforcement_inhibit_all.unmapped: The assistance port recomputes ModType-44 inhibition from owned outfits instead of reading this cache; independently sampled cache bytes cannot reproduce the same port state.

g_government_defs.why: The original table is fixed at 0x100 entries. The port sizes its vector from the data and range-checks against it, so the host sizes it to the original's extent.

g_ship_states.why: Fixed 0x40-slot array; element 0 is the player (the port's GameState.player aliases ships_[0]).

g_weapon_defs.why: 0x100 entries indexed by the zero-based weapon id (the original range-checks ids against 0x100, e.g. 0x0046ea86); the port's vector is indexed by resource id - 0x80, the same index.

g_ship_class_defs.why: 0x300 entries indexed by the zero-based ship id; the port's vector is indexed by resource id - 0x80, the same index.

g_outfit_defs.why: 0x200 entries indexed by the zero-based outfit id.

g_outfit_owned_count.why: The player's owned count per zero-based outfit id (0x200 shorts).

g_player_max_armor_cache.unmapped: Ship_ComputeShipMaxArmor (0x004637a0) reads the player's lazily cached max armor, while the port's NovaAi_ComputeMaxArmorPoints recomputes it from the class and outfits; the invented cache is independent of the invented class, so the run cannot be compared faithfully.

g_system_defs_ptr.why: Original fixed 0x800 system table; nav entries are zero-based stellar indexes.

g_stellar_defs.why: Original fixed 0x800 stellar table; vector indices match original stellar indexes.

reinforcement_inhibited.unmapped: The assistance port recomputes government-class inhibition from owned outfits instead of reading independently sampled cached bytes.

0x0040c790.why: Port returns a stellar resource id; original returns its zero-based index. Both return -1 for no selection.
